condition: Recurrent falls in an elderly woman on antihypertensives

patient_persona.description: Hajah Kalsom binti Awang, 78, female, widow living with her daughter in Kuala Terengganu; hypertension and diabetes. Slow, soft voice, a little hard of hearing; daughter adds details.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Wong Jun Ming, Malaysian Chinese man in his 30s, family medicine doctor at a Terengganu klinik kesihatan geriatric clinic. Patient, speaks loudly and clearly; Malay with English terms.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mak Hajah, saya dengar mak jatuh lagi minggu lepas. Jatuh kat mana?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Dalam bilik air, doktor. Pagi-pagi bangun nak ambil wuduk, tiba-tiba gelap mata, terus jatuh. Lutut lebam, bruise besar.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Masa jatuh tu, mak pengsan ke, atau sedar je?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Sedar. Cuma rasa pening berpusing sekejap bila bangun dari katil, like spinning. Anak saya yang angkat.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Tahun ni dah berapa kali jatuh, mak?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Tiga kali, doktor. Anak saya kata empat, saya pun dah lupa, memory tak berapa baik.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Saya check tekanan darah baring dan berdiri ya. Baring 148 atas 80, berdiri turun ke 118 atas 70. Turun banyak bila berdiri, postural hypotension.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Tekanan darah saya kan tinggi? Kenapa pula rendah?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Masa baring tinggi, tapi bila bangun dia jatuh mendadak. Ubat darah tinggi mak ada tiga jenis, amlodipine, perindopril, dan hydrochlorothiazide.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Saya nak stop hydrochlorothiazide, sebab dia buat kencing banyak dan tekanan darah jatuh. Yang lain teruskan dulu.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ubat gula saya pula, glibenclamide, kadang-kadang saya rasa menggeletar, berpeluh petang-petang.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Itu tanda gula rendah, hypoglycaemia. Pada umur mak, glibenclamide tak sesuai. Saya tukar kepada gliclazide 40mg, sekali pagi.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Mata saya pun kabur, doktor. Cermin mata dah lama tak tukar.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mata kabur pun sebab jatuh. Saya refer ke eye clinic. Bila bangun tidur, sit at the edge of the bed for one minute, baru berdiri perlahan-lahan.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Bilik air rumah kami licin, doktor. Lantai jubin.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Pasang pemegang kat dinding bilik air, letak tikar getah, dan lampu malam. Saya rujuk physiotherapist untuk latihan imbangan. Jumpa lagi dua minggu, check tekanan darah.

condition: Hip fracture after a fall, pre-discharge rehabilitation talk

patient_persona.description: Mr. Lee Ah Kow, 82, male, retired coffee shop owner in Ipoh; fractured left hip, had a hemiarthroplasty five days ago. Stubborn, humorous, Cantonese-flavoured Mandarin.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Nurul Huda binti Azman, Malay woman in her 30s, orthopaedic medical officer at an Ipoh hospital. Encouraging, firm; English with Mandarin and Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Uncle Lee, 早安. How's the pain today? Scale zero to ten?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 早安医生。今天好一点，大概四分。可是那个 physio 每天叫我走路，好辛苦。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I know it's tiring, uncle. But walking early is the most important thing after hip surgery. It prevents clots and pneumonia, 肺炎.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我八十二岁了，走不走都一样啦。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 不一样, uncle. Those who walk early go home faster and are more independent. You want to go back to your kopitiam friends, right?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 哈哈，对啊，每天早上都要去喝 kopi O 看报纸。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Then must walk with the frame first. Physio 说你昨天走了二十米. Good progress.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我什么时候可以回家？My son is in KL，家里只有我和我太太。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Maybe two or three more days. But at home, need some changes. 你家的厕所是蹲的还是坐的?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 蹲的。楼上还有房间，我们睡楼上。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Squatting is not allowed for now, the new hip can dislocate. Need a commode chair, 便盆椅, and please sleep downstairs for at least six weeks.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 这么麻烦……那我太太一个人照顾我吗？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I'll ask the social worker to talk to your son. Maybe a maid or day care for a few weeks.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Also, your fall was because of weak bones, 骨头很脆. We'll start calcium and vitamin D, and a yearly zoledronic acid drip to strengthen the bones.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 一年打一次针？那还好。以前我 fall down 都没事的。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Because the bones are thin now, 骨质疏松. When you go home, no loose rugs, good lighting, use the walking frame always.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 好啦好啦，我听你的。

condition: Fall with head injury in an elderly man on warfarin

patient_persona.description: Mrs. Mary Thomas, 58, female, daughter and caregiver of Mr. George Thomas, 84, who has atrial fibrillation on warfarin; retired nurse from Petaling Jaya. Knowledgeable, concerned, speaks crisp Malaysian English with some Malay.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Mohd Rizal bin Hashim, Malay man in his 40s, emergency physician at a Selangor hospital. Focused, clear; English with Malay.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor, Daddy fell in the hall last night around eleven. He hit his head on the side table. Dia kata okay, but he's on warfarin, so I brought him in.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: You did the right thing. Mr. Thomas, do you remember the fall? Any loss of consciousness?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: He says he remembers everything, but he seems a bit slower this morning, lambat sikit. Repeating the same question twice.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: That change is important. Any vomiting, headache, weakness on one side?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Headache yes, he took Panadol. Muntah sekali pagi tadi. No weakness that I can see.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: His INR today is 3.6, higher than the target of two to three. Dos warfarin ada ubah baru-baru ni?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: The clinic increased it two weeks ago, from 3mg to 4mg daily. And he's been minum teh herba dari kawan dia, tongkat ali or something.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Herbal products can interfere with warfarin. Kecederaan kepala, umur lebih 65, and anticoagulation, he needs a CT brain now.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Please. Masa saya kerja dulu, I've seen many cases like this in the ward.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: CT shows a small subdural haematoma, a thin bleed on the right side. No midline shift. I've called the neurosurgery team.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Oh God. Will he need surgery?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Not at this size, maybe. First we reverse the warfarin with vitamin K and prothrombin complex concentrate. Lepas tu repeat CT in six hours.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: What about his AF? If we stop warfarin, won't he get a stroke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: That's the balance. For now bleeding risk is higher. Neurosurgery and cardiology will decide when to restart, maybe in a few weeks.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay. I'll stay with him. Should I call my brother in Singapore?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Yes, please inform family. He'll be in the high dependency ward. We'll update you after the next scan. Teh herba tu stop dulu, okay?

condition: Fear of falling and deconditioning after a fall

patient_persona.description: Mdm. Tan Gek Hoon, 76, female, retired hawker living alone in a flat in Bukit Mertajam, Penang; fell at a wet market three months ago. Anxious, soft-spoken, Hokkien-flavoured Mandarin.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Sharifah Nabilah binti Syed Omar, Malay woman in her 40s, family medicine specialist at a Penang klinik kesihatan. Gentle; English and Malay with simple Mandarin.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Auntie Tan, 你好. Since the fall three months ago, how are you managing at home?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 医生，我现在都不敢出门了。怕又 fall down。每天都在家里坐着看 TV。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I understand. After a fall, many elderly become afraid. But sitting all day makes the legs weaker, 脚会越来越没力.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 对啊，我现在上楼梯都要拉着扶手，以前我每天走去 pasar 的。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Let me test. 不用手，从椅子站起来五次. Okay, you took 18 seconds. That shows weak leg muscles.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 那怎么办？我一个人住，女儿在 Singapore 工作。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: The best treatment is exercise. I'll refer you to physio for a strength and balance programme, twice a week, at this klinik.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我怎么来？我不会开车，搭 bas 又怕。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Your neighbour's daughter brought you today, right? Maybe she can help. Also boleh guna community transport for elderly, I'll ask our nurse.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 在家里可以做什么运动吗？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Yes. 扶着厨房的桌子, stand on your toes ten times. Sit to stand from a chair ten times, 早上和晚上.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 这个我可以做。那我脚底有时候麻麻的, numb numb, 会不会是这个原因跌倒？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Could be. Your sugar is high, HbA1c 8.6. 糖尿病会让脚麻. I'll check your feet sensation now.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Sensation reduced on both feet. So wear shoes with good grip, 在家里也要穿. No slippers that slide off.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我在家都穿 selipar……好，我叫女儿买一双鞋子给我。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Also, we'll get you a personal alarm, 跌倒的时候可以按. Come back in one month, tell me how many times you went out.

condition: Fall at night in an elderly man with nocturia and sleeping pills

patient_persona.description: Encik Osman bin Daud, 80, male, retired rubber estate worker in Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan; enlarged prostate. Talkative, proud, dislikes being fussed over.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Chan Yoke Lin, Malaysian Chinese woman in her 50s, family medicine specialist at a Seremban clinic. Straight-talking, warm; Malay with English terms.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Pak Osman, anak pak cik telefon saya, kata pak cik jatuh tengah malam minggu lepas.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Alah, sikit je, doktor. Saya bangun nak kencing, gelap, tersadung selipar. No problem one.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Malam bangun kencing berapa kali?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Tiga empat kali. Prostat saya kan besar. Kalau tak bangun, basah katil.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ada makan ubat tidur? Ubat tenang?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ada, anak saya beli dari farmasi, kata ubat tidur. Satu biji sebelum tidur. Kalau tak, saya tak lena.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Boleh tunjuk botol dia? Ini diphenhydramine. It makes you drowsy and confused at night, dan boleh buat susah kencing.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Oh, patutlah saya rasa berat kepala, heavy head, bila bangun malam.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Saya nak pak cik stop ubat ni. Untuk tidur, kita cuba cara lain. Jangan tidur siang lama-lama, kurangkan kopi petang.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kopi O petang tu dah jadi kebiasaan, doktor. Tapi kalau kena kurang, saya cuba lah.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Untuk prostat, pak cik makan tamsulosin 0.4mg sekarang, kan? Minum air banyak sebelum Maghrib, lepas Isyak kurangkan.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kurang minum malam? Nanti kering tekak.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Hirup sikit-sikit je. Letak lampu tidur dari bilik ke tandas, dan urinal botol tepi katil kalau perlu.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Guna botol tu macam orang sakit pulak. Saya malu, doktor, embarrassing.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Lebih baik guna botol daripada patah pinggul, pak cik. A hip fracture at eighty, susah nak jalan balik.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Betul juga. Kawan saya dulu patah pinggul, lepas tu terus terlantar. Baiklah, saya dengar cakap doktor.

condition: Polypharmacy medication review in an elderly diabetic

patient_persona.description: Mr. Goh Seng Huat, 74, male, retired lorry driver in Klang; diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, knee pain; brings a plastic bag of medicines. Cheerful, slightly confused about drug names.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Ruhana binti Abdul Latif, Malay woman in her 40s, family medicine specialist running a medication review clinic in Klang. Organised, patient; English with Mandarin and Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Uncle Goh, today we check all your medicines, 所有的药. You brought them all?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 带来了，这一袋都是。有些是医院的，有些是 private 诊所的，有些是 pharmacy 买的。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Okay, let's lay them out. Metformin, amlodipine, perindopril, atorvastatin, aspirin, omeprazole, and this one, diclofenac. Who gave diclofenac?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 这个是 private 诊所给的，脚痛吃的。一天两次。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Diclofenac with your kidneys is not good. Your creatinine went up this year, eGFR 48. 跟 aspirin 一起吃, stomach bleeding risk.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 那脚痛怎么办？不吃会痛到走不动。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Paracetamol 1 gram, three times a day is safer. And diclofenac gel on the knee. 涂的，不是吃的.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 好。那这个 Chinese medicine 呢？我儿子从 Taiwan 带回来的，说对 diabetes 好。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Please stop that one first, 先停. Some herbal products can affect sugar and kidneys. 我们不知道里面有什么.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 还有这个，我每天吃两粒 metformin，早上一粒，晚上一粒。可是医院又开了这盒，我不知道是一样的。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Aiyo, this box is also metformin, just different brand. So you've been taking double dose, four tablets a day.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 真的吗？难怪我常常肚子不舒服，拉肚子。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: That's probably why. From now, metformin 500mg twice a day only, from one box. Throw the other away, or give back to pharmacy.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 药这么多，我常常搞乱。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I'll ask the pharmacist to prepare a pill box, 药盒, with morning and night sections. Your daughter can fill it weekly.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 好啊，这样方便多了。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Also bring all medicines every visit, 包括 private 诊所的药. So total now seven, down from ten. Next month we check sugar and kidney again.

condition: Medication review with anticholinergic burden and constipation

patient_persona.description: Mrs. Saraswathy a/p Kandasamy, 72, female, retired kindergarten teacher in Taiping, Perak; on multiple medicines from different specialists. Polite, organised, keeps a medication list.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Lim Kah Hock, Malaysian Chinese man in his 50s, geriatrician at a Taiping hospital. Thoughtful, slow-paced; English with some Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mrs. Saraswathy, I see you're seeing four clinics: cardiology, urology, psychiatry and the klinik kesihatan. Can we go through your list together?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes, doctor. I wrote everything here. Fourteen types of medicine. Morning seven, night five, and two for when needed.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Very organised. You mentioned constipation, mulut kering and feeling blur. Since when?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Since last year. Every morning mouth kering like sandpaper. Constipation also, sometimes five days tak buang air besar.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Some of your medicines have anticholinergic effects: oxybutynin untuk pundi kencing, amitriptyline for sleep, and chlorpheniramine you take for itch.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: The oxybutynin is from urology, for my frequent urine. Amitriptyline from psychiatry for my mood and sleep.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Together, these can cause dry mouth, constipation, and even confusion or falls in older people, orang tua.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Oh dear. My daughter says I'm quite pelupa recently. I thought it's just old age.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: It could be partly the medicines. I'd like to switch oxybutynin to mirabegron 25mg, which doesn't have that effect.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: And the amitriptyline? Without it I cannot sleep at all, tak boleh tidur langsung.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: We can taper it slowly, perlahan-lahan, and I'll discuss with your psychiatrist about sertraline instead, which is gentler. Jangan stop tiba-tiba.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay. The chlorpheniramine I take because of itchy skin at night.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Your skin is very dry, kulit kering sangat. Use emollient cream twice daily, and if needed, cetirizine 10mg instead, less drowsy.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Fourteen medicines, doctor, sometimes I feel like I'm makan ubat for breakfast.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I understand. After this we'll be at eleven, and hopefully fewer later. I'll write one clear letter to all your doctors.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Thank you, doctor. Nobody ever looked at everything together like this.

condition: Polypharmacy with over-the-counter supplements and warfarin

patient_persona.description: Encik Ramli bin Yaakob, 69, male, retired police officer in Alor Setar, Kedah; atrial fibrillation on warfarin, gout, hypertension. Talkative, confident, likes "natural" products.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Tan Siew Ling, Malaysian Chinese woman in her 30s, clinical pharmacist-trained family medicine doctor in Alor Setar. Friendly, detail-oriented; Malay with English terms.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Encik Ramli, INR encik bulan ni 4.2, tinggi. Target kita dua ke tiga. Ada perubahan apa-apa sejak bulan lepas?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Tak ada ubah ubat, doktor. Cuma saya ada makan supplement sikit, the natural ones. Fish oil, habbatus sauda, dan kunyit kapsul.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Suplemen tu dah berapa lama?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kunyit tu baru sebulan. Kawan surau cakap bagus untuk joint. Minyak ikan dah lama.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Kunyit dan minyak ikan dua-dua boleh tambah kesan warfarin, darah jadi lebih cair. Ada gusi berdarah, lebam, atau kencing merah?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Gusi ada berdarah sikit masa gosok gigi. Lebam kat lengan pun ada, bruises, saya ingat terlanggar pintu.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Itu tanda warfarin terlalu kuat. Malam ni skip satu dos warfarin, esok sambung 3mg macam biasa, dan stop kunyit kapsul.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kunyit dalam masakan pun kena stop ke? Isteri saya masak gulai setiap hari.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Kunyit dalam masakan tak apa, jumlah dia sikit. The problem is the high-dose capsule.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Satu lagi, colchicine untuk gout, encik makan hari-hari ke?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Hari-hari, dua biji. Dari klinik swasta, dah setahun.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Colchicine setiap hari pada dos tu, dengan buah pinggang encik, boleh buat lemah otot dan cirit-birit. Untuk cegah gout jangka panjang, allopurinol lebih sesuai.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Saya memang selalu cirit-birit, doktor. Saya ingat sebab food poisoning.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mungkin sebab colchicine. Saya mula allopurinol 100mg sehari, colchicine turun ke satu biji sehari untuk tiga bulan je, lepas tu stop.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Banyak betul ubat nak ingat. Boleh tulis?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Saya print jadual ubat baru. Datang semula seminggu untuk check INR. Setiap kali nak makan apa-apa suplemen, tanya kami dulu.

condition: Deprescribing in a frail elderly woman with dementia

patient_persona.description: Mr. Kenny Chong Wai Mun, 50, male, son and caregiver of Mdm. Chong Siew Lan, 88, who has moderate dementia and lives with him in Cheras; logistics manager. Tired, frank, English with Cantonese particles and Malay.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Aishah binti Mohd Shukri, Malay woman in her 40s, geriatrician at a KL hospital. Compassionate, unhurried; English with Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mr. Chong, thanks for coming. Your mother is on eleven medicines. As her dementia progresses, some may not help her anymore. Boleh kita bincang?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Please, doctor. She hates swallowing pills. Every morning is a fight, she spits them out. The maid also struggling, kesian dia.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Let's look at what matters most now. Her goals are comfort, eating well, sleeping well, not falling. Do you agree?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes. She's 88 already. Saya tak nak seksa dia with so many tablets.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Atorvastatin for cholesterol is for long-term heart protection over years. Pada tahap ni, benefit is very small. We can stop it.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay. What about the diabetes medicine? Her sugar is quite okay now, she makan sikit je.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Her HbA1c is 6.1, too tight for her age. Low sugar is more dangerous, can cause falls and confusion. Let's stop gliclazide, keep only metformin at a lower dose.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: She also takes donepezil. Is it still useful? Some days dia tak kenal saya pun.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Donepezil gives modest benefit. Some families continue, some stop. Since she's losing weight and has poor appetite, it may be worth a trial off.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: If we stop and she becomes worse?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Watch for more agitation or confusion in the first two weeks. If so, we restart. It's reversible.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Alright. And the calcium tablet, so big, she always tercekik.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: We can stop it, or change to a chewable or liquid form. Her aspirin, she had no heart attack or stroke before, right?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No, the GP just started it because of her age, I think. Takde sebab lain.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Then aspirin can stop too, less bleeding risk. So from eleven, down to six. Jauh lebih senang.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Wah, thank you doctor. It feels like we're finally thinking about what she wants.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: That's exactly the point. Come back in one month, and call us earlier kalau ada apa-apa yang risau.

condition: Medication review for a stroke survivor with swallowing difficulty

patient_persona.description: Puan Rosmah binti Harun, 45, female, daughter and caregiver of Encik Harun bin Said, 76, who had a stroke six months ago with swallowing problems; nursery owner in Taiping, Perak. Tired, organised, emotional.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Mohan a/l Pillai, Malaysian Indian man in his 50s, rehabilitation physician at a Perak hospital. Kind, patient; Malay with English terms.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Puan Rosmah, macam mana ayah sekarang? Makan ubat macam mana?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Susah, doktor. Ayah choke bila telan biji ubat. Saya hancurkan semua, campur dengan bubur. Tapi dia kata pahit sangat.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ada ubat yang tak boleh dihancurkan, cannot crush. Boleh saya tengok senarai?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ini senarai dia. Aspirin, clopidogrel, atorvastatin, amlodipine, metformin, nifedipine SR, omeprazole, dan vitamin B.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Nifedipine SR ni slow release. Kalau dihancurkan, semua ubat keluar sekaligus, tekanan darah boleh jatuh mendadak. Itu bahaya.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ya Allah, saya tak tahu. Patutlah ayah kadang-kadang pening lepas makan ubat pagi, blood pressure drop.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Kita boleh stop nifedipine. Dia dah ada amlodipine, dua ubat sama jenis. Tekanan darah dia sekarang 128 atas 76, cukup baik.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Aspirin dan clopidogrel, kena dua-dua ke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Lepas stroke, dua-dua biasanya untuk tiga minggu pertama je. Dah enam bulan, cukup satu, clopidogrel 75mg.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Alhamdulillah, kurang dua biji. Metformin tu besar sangat, doktor.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ada bentuk sirap metformin atau tablet kecil dos rendah. Gula dia pun dah OK, HbA1c 6.8.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Speech therapist ada kata ayah kena guna air pekat, thickened. Ubat boleh campur dengan air pekat ke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Boleh, kebanyakan ubat boleh campur dengan jelly atau thickener. Pharmacist akan tunjuk macam mana. Duduk tegak masa telan, dan tiga puluh minit selepas makan.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Terima kasih, doktor. Saya selalu rasa bersalah, takut buat silap.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Puan dah jaga ayah dengan sangat baik. Soalan macam ni penting. Jumpa lagi sebulan, and please take care of yourself too.
